condition_description: Sender display name implies an internal/official identity (ICT, Registrar, Bursary, Security, brand name...) but the sender's actual email domain is not in the university's allow-list.
Subject or body contains urgency and/or credential-harvesting language (e.g. 'verify', 'suspended', 'confirm your password', '24 hours').
The Reply-To address domain differs from the From address domain.
The URL's host is a raw IPv4 address rather than a domain name.
The URL contains an '@' sign before the real host (classic userinfo obfuscation trick).
The host contains a recognisable brand token (e.g. 'crescent') but is not on the university's allow-list - a look-alike/misspelt domain.
The host has more than 3 dot-separated labels (excessive/suspicious sub-domaining).
The URL scheme is not HTTPS.
The host ends in a suspicious/free top-level domain (.tk, .ml, .ga, .cf, .gq, .xyz, .top, .work).
The login form's 'action' attribute posts to a different host than the page's own (declared) host.
The page contains one or more hidden <input> fields inside the login form (silent extra-data harvesting).
The page's host is not on the university's allow-list of legitimate domains.
